analysis: The method getExtension takes a String filename and calls filename.substring(filename.lastIndexOf('.') + 1). The lastIndexOf('.') method returns the index of the last occurrence of '.' or -1 if none. Adding 1 yields a beginIndex value that is always between 0 and the length of the string (inclusive). Specifically: if no dot exists, beginIndex = 0; if dot is at the last character, beginIndex = length; otherwise, beginIndex is between 1 and length-1. Thus, beginIndex is never negative and never greater than the string's length. The only exception documented for substring is IndexOutOfBoundsException for negative or too-large beginIndex, so this condition is fully avoided in the calling context. Note: A null filename would cause a NullPointerException before the substring call, but that exception is not declared in substring's documentation and is not part of this analysis.
remark: The trigger scenario for IndexOutOfBoundsException (beginIndex negative or > length) cannot occur because filename.lastIndexOf('.') + 1 always yields a value in the range [0, length], satisfying the valid range for beginIndex. Therefore, the exception is entirely avoided in this code.
